To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the current Standard-Model prediction for the muon ( g − 2 ) is 3.5 ± 0.7 × 10 − 10, which is significantly smaller than the experimental value 11.1 × 10 −10 ( 0.54 % ), and that the theoretical uncertainty should be reduced by about a factor of two by the end of this year, which will lead to a 3.0 σ difference.
the current difference between theory and experiment in the muon (anomalous) magnetic moment is (a_μ - a_μ^SM)exp - (a_μ-a_μ^SM)^SM = (25.1 ± 8.0)×10−10.
the Standard-Model prediction for the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon has an uncertainty of ±49 × 10-11, and that a 3.7σ deviation from the experimental result is observed.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the Standard Model prediction of the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon, and with the improvement of the Standard Model prediction for the muon g-2, which is the difference between the experimental and the Standard Model theoretical values.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the current discrepancy between the Standard-Model prediction and the Brookhaven experiment is at the 3 - 3.5 standard-deviation level, and that the Standard Model is not yet excluded at the 95% confidence level.
the current difference between theory and experiment is a 3-4 sigma effect.

, while the present discrepancy between the Standard Model prediction and the Brookhaven experiment result cannot be considered as a discovery of New Physics, the discrepancy is large enough to be a strong motivation for a new experiment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Standard Model prediction for the muon anomalous magnetic moment is in a state of flux.
we have made substantial progress in reducing the theoretical uncertainty in the Standard Model prediction of the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon.

the current Standard-Model value is not yet sufficiently precise to claim that the discrepancy between experiment and theory is significant.
